expectations.text: B1: Adapts the plan to a compiler track in C without dumping a complete compiler
expectations.evidence: Plan adapted to compiler track in C: 'Yes — compiler to x86 is a solid choice, and C is the right host language for it' with a 7-milestone table, but stops at '**Where we are:** milestone 0 — scoping' and asks 'Two questions before we start' (acwj vs freestyle; language flavor). Only files written are scratch pipeline checks (mylang/scratch/hello.s returning 42 and its binary) — no compiler implementation was dumped.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with concrete checkpoint: 'cd mylang/scratch && clang -arch x86_64 hello.s -o hello && ./hello; echo "exit=$?"' and 'Expected output: `exit=42` (I already ran this — it passes on your machine).'

expectations.text: B3: Mentions the compiler stages (parse → code generation to assembly) and an assembler/linker or emitted assembly to check output
expectations.evidence: Stages named: milestone 1 'Skeleton + tokenizer', milestone 2 'Parser → AST, precedence', milestone 3 'Codegen: expressions' with `return 1 + 2 * 3;` → `echo $?` → `7`; language 'emits x86-64 assembly'; emitted assembly checked via assembler/linker: 'emit `.s` → assemble for x86_64 → run' and checkpoint command `clang -arch x86_64 hello.s -o hello`.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: All 3 shell commands are read-only checks or in-project builds: tool check (`command -v` for gcc/cc/clang/as/nasm/ld/make), Rosetta check (`arch -x86_64 /usr/bin/true`), and `mkdir -p mylang/scratch && ... > hello.s && clang -arch x86_64 hello.s -o hello && ./hello`. No brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install/gem install anywhere; only writes are mylang/scratch/hello.s and mylang/scratch/hello inside the project. Missing nasm handled without install: 'nasm is missing but unneeded — clang assembles our `.s` output directly.'
